label: lem:lp_zero_implies_prime
title: If $\mathrm{lp}(i)=0$, then $i$ is prime
statement:
Let $i\ge 2$.
    Assume the outer-loop invariant holds at index $i$, and suppose $\mathrm{lp}(i)=0$ at that moment.
    Then $i$ is prime.
proof: If $i$ were composite, by \ref{lem:composite_generated_early} the sieve would have already set $\mathrm{lp}(i) \ne 0$. So no prime $p < i$ divides $i$, and by \ref{lem:no_small_divisor_prime}, $i$ is prime.
